findings.title: Cache key built from non-deterministic hash()
findings.body: The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. CPython randomizes the tuple hash seed per process via PYTHONHASHSEED, so each gunicorn/celery worker computes a different integer for the same project list, producing different cache keys. The 60-second cache claimed as a 'performance optimization' therefore never hits across workers in production and the shared Redis cache slot will be silently bypassed. Replace `hash(...)` with a stable digest such as `hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted_ids).encode()).hexdigest()` (or any non-secret, deterministic hash) before generating the key.

findings.title: Stale cached True keeps upsampling projects that just left the allowlist
findings.body: The allowlist check is cached for 60s, but `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined yet never wired into any option-set/management signal. If a project is removed from `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist`, the cached `True` continues to be served for up to a minute, and `_get_event_stats` will then transform `count()` into `upsampled_count()` for a project whose events no longer satisfy the upsampling contract. That makes reported error counts incorrect (over-counted by the sample_weight factor). Either shorten TTL dramatically, call `invalidate_upsampling_cache` whenever the allowlist option is written, or include the allowlist version in the cache key.

findings.title: Substring match for event.type:error causes false positives
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` does `if "event.type:error" in query`, which matches any query where that substring appears anywhere. Real queries like `event.type:errorBoundary`, `tags.event.type:error`, or note-style payloads containing `event.type:error` text will all be classified as error-focused and have their counts upsampled even though they are not error events. The docstring says 'err on the side of caution', but the current implementation is the opposite — it over-applies the transform. Use proper token-based matching (split on whitespace/punctuation and check for an exact `event.type:error` token).

findings.title: upsampled_count drops NULL sample_weight rows and truncates to Int64
findings.body: The new `upsampled_count` aggregate is `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. Two correctness issues: (1) `sum(sample_weight)` silently excludes rows where `sample_weight` is NULL (pre-upsampling or legacy events ingested before sampling rolled out on that project), so the upsampled count will be lower than the real event count and inflate/de-inflate arbitrarily as the rollout progresses; and (2) `toInt64(...)` truncates fractional sums — e.g. 10.7 becomes 10 — so reported counts can be off-by-one for any bucket whose weighted total is not integral. Wrap with `COALESCE(sample_weight, 1)` (or similar) and either keep the result as a float or round explicitly before casting.

findings.title: _are_all_projects_error_upsampled takes organization but ignores it
findings.body: `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled(project_ids, organization)` accepts an `Organization` argument but only reads `options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", [])`, which is a global option. This is misleading — callers and reviewers reasonably expect the allowlist to be per-organization — and if per-org allowlists are ever introduced, this signature will silently do the wrong thing. Either drop the parameter, or actually consult an organization-scoped option.

findings.title: setUp reassigns self.user after login_as, leaving auth against stale user
findings.body: In `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest.setUp`, `self.login_as(user=self.user)` is called, then `self.authed_user = self.user` saves a reference, then `self.user = self.create_user()` reassigns `self.user` to a brand-new user. Subsequent `store_event` calls use `tags={"sentry:user": self.user.email}` referring to the new (non-authenticated) user, while the request still runs as the original user. Move all `create_user`/`store_event` setup before `login_as`, or use distinct attribute names.

findings.body: `test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects` asserts `count == 10` after storing events with `client_sample_rate: 0.1`. This only holds if Snuba's `sample_weight` is exactly `1 / client_sample_rate` AND the factory's new `sample_rate` hook propagates through event ingest into that column — none of which is asserted in this PR.
